definition: Recovering or restoring video from degraded, compressed, or incomplete input — the temporal analogue of image reconstruction.
details: Recovering or restoring video from degraded, compressed, or incomplete input — the temporal analogue of image reconstruction.

explainer.lead: Video reconstruction restores usable footage from degraded, compressed, or incomplete input. It matters because much real-world video arrives damaged or heavily compressed and must be repaired before anything downstream can use it.

tiers.eli5: It's like taking a blurry, glitchy home movie and cleaning it up so you can actually see what happened.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply it to remove compression artifacts and fill missing frames before analysis or upscaling. A common pitfall is over-restoring: the model invents plausible detail that was never in the source.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as recovering a clean video sequence from a degraded observation, the temporal analogue of image reconstruction; quality is limited by how much information the degradation has irreversibly removed.

explainer.example: A heavily compressed security clip is fed through a reconstruction model to recover sharper frames of a passing car.
